title: Changing UK Family Adventure
welcome_lead: UK family life keeps changing. Let's track it. 🏠
meta_desc: Family & Identity Adventure 3 — KS3 Sociology on how the UK family has changed over decades.
final_note: You learned how UK families have changed since the 1950s.

concepts.def: Number of babies born per year

walkthroughs.body_html:
In the 1950s most families were nuclear, mum often stayed home.

Today: diversity rules. Many shapes are normal.

• Divorce rose after 1969 law made it easier.
  • More people cohabit instead of marrying.
  • Civil partnerships from 2004, same-sex marriage 2014.
  • People marry older — average UK age now over 30.

The UK birth rate has fallen — about 1.6 babies per woman now.

Reasons: women have careers, cost of housing, choice.

Result: smaller families, more diverse households. 👨‍👩‍👧
